text:
Alex: Heads up — started seeing p99 spikes on prod when concurrency > 400. Suspect KV cache evictions interacting with kernel selection. Dumping profiler now, will paste logs. :eyes:
Maria: Confirmed, saw the same at ~12:10 UTC. p95 stayed OK but p99 jumps. Microbatch size is 16 on that pool, seq length shifted heavier (more long-chats).
PerfBot: CI profiler summary (id: 1846509878)
```
concurrency: 450
microbatch_size: 16
kernel_selected: fast-attn-v2
fallback_kernel: slow-attn (triggered)
p95: 84ms
p99: 612ms
kv_hit_rate: 0.67
evictions_per_sec: 120
kv_eviction_latency_tail_ms: 200-800
note: kernel fallback aligns with windows of high eviction churn and increased KV miss latency
```
Sid: Interesting — looks like eviction churn spikes cause more cache misses which increase effective sequence length (KV fetches + fallback path). Two levers: microbatch sizing and kernel hinting. Smaller microbatches reduce queuing but lower throughput.
Jo: Ran a quick heatmap of eviction frequency by KV shard (canary pool). Paste below:
```
Shard  | evict/sec @ conc=450
-------------------------
shard-00 | 4
shard-01 | 7
shard-02 | 35  <-- hot/victim
shard-03 | 3
shard-04 | 46  <-- hot/victim
shard-05 | 2
shard-06 | 18
shard-07 | 5
```
Jo: `redwood profile --targets=kv --heatmap --concurrency=450` produced that. Looks like a couple of shards are thrashing and causing global stall windows. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Maria: Proposed experiment:
- Canary pool A: microbatch_size=8, kernel_hint=stable-attn, cache_ttl_hot=300s, kv_pin_top=10
- Canary pool B: microbatch_size=16, same as prod but aggressive prefetch for hot keys
Measure p95/p99, throughput, and tokens/sec for 1 hour. Expected: microbatch=8 -> p99 down ~2.3x, throughput -10-20%.
Alex: Sounds good. I'll schedule canary rollout at 13:00 UTC and monitor. @PerfBot please run a 1h trace with sampling=1% on both pools after rollout. :wrench:
PerfBot: Scheduled trace job id=tb-1846509900. Will post results to this thread once finished.
Sid: Quick thought on kernel selection: we should add a brief hysteresis window before switching kernels on a per-worker basis. Right now a burst of eviction misses flips kernel and cold-path hits immediately. Add a 60s smoothing would avoid oscillation.
Maria: Agree. Also instrument kv_hit_rate by prefix so we can auto-pin the top N prefixes per shard. That would reduce hot-key evictions and keep fast kernel stable.
Alex: If canary shows improvement, we'll roll to prod with kernel-hysteresis + microbatch=8 for that pool. Keep in mind cost/throughput tradeoff.
PerfBot: Trace job finished (id=tb-1846509900). Summary:
```
poolA (mb=8): p95=70ms p99=250ms throughput=112k tok/s
poolB (mb=16+prefetch): p95=82ms p99=490ms throughput=128k tok/s
kv_hit_rate_poolA=0.82 kv_hit_rate_poolB=0.69
```
Jo: Nice — poolA reduced p99 by ~2x at ~12.5% throughput drop. Heatmap after canary shows eviction_per_sec for hot shards down from 46->9.
Maria: Next actions:
- Add kernel hysteresis (60s) + metric to alert if hysteresis prevents needed fallback for >5min
- Implement hot-prefix pinning autopilot (start with top 5 per shard)
- Short-term: reduce microbatch to 8 on high-concurrency pools (config flag)
Alex: I'll open the rollout PR and schedule the kernel-hysteresis change. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
